Operations

How work is actually controlled

Automation without control is just faster disorder. Every document passes five gates. At each one something is enforced, something is written to the record, and there is a named path for when it does not go to plan. Six workflow stages, five control gates — dispatch and archive close under Gate 5.

Gate 1

Registration

Enforced

A reference is minted once. Category and subcategory set on arrival.

Recorded

Responsible unit, supporting unit, priority and both SLA clocks — derived, not typed.

Exception

Unrecognised category lands on a named default, never on whatever sorts first.

Gate 2

Acknowledgement

Enforced

Receipt confirmed before work starts, within the acknowledgement window.

Recorded

A receipt in the ledger: who, when, from where, and the key that stops a double entry.

Exception

Not acknowledged in time → it ages into the SLA watch list.

Gate 3

Action

Enforced

Work happens in one queue, against the record, with the completion clock in view.

Recorded

Comments, updates and evidence attach to the record as the officer works.

Exception

Waiting on something outside the unit → blocked, and visibly so.

Gate 4

Decision

Enforced

Approve, return, reject or escalate — a decision is one of four things.

Recorded

The decision, the decider and the trail behind it, available to audit.

Exception

Beyond the unit’s authority → escalated to the executive decision hub.

Gate 5

Dispatch & closure

Enforced

Outward mail on a branded template; closure requires a dispatch outcome.

Recorded

Dispatch receipt, closure, then archive under a retention class with a date.

Exception

No-dispatch is an outcome too — recorded with its reason, not left open.

How it was built, and what comes next

A frontend-for-backend strategy — and the phase after it

What it bought

Capability without waiting, and without a capital programme

  • ✓No application servers to license or maintain — no framework, no middleware.
  • ✓Deployed as static files — nothing to keep alive between the interface and the flows.
  • ✓The gap in backend infrastructure was closed rather than waited on.
  • ✓Delivered on operating budget, using platforms the Agency already licenses.
What the next phase needs

From correspondence handling to enterprise content management

  • →A governed repository — contracts, policies, project records and evidence, with versioning and disposition.
  • →Records controls and legal hold enforced enterprise-wide, not declared.
  • →Linkage to ERP on shared identifiers, so a transaction and its evidence find each other.
  • →Storage, search and integration sized for the whole Agency.
NITDA · DGO Digital Ops8 / 9
The next rung

Opening the channel to the public

Every level so far improved how the Agency handles correspondence once it arrives. The next extends the same governed record outward — to the person who sent it.

01

Submit from anywhere

With attachments, identity confirmed by a one-time code to the sender’s own address before anything enters the registry.

02

Watch the reference move

Received, in review, action required, closed — the same states the officers work in, shown to the person waiting.

03

Respond or withdraw

The correspondence stays a conversation rather than a one-way deposit.

04

Close the loop

Dispatch receipt, closure and retention — the citizen sees the outcome, the Agency keeps the evidence.
